record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove a uniqueness theorem for maximal surfaces under only the dominant energy condition, filling the gap between known uniqueness under the timelike convergence condition and uniqueness in spacetimes with a timelike Killing vector?

evidence.quote: Maximal Cauchy surfaces are known to be unique if the timelike convergence condition (TCC) is satisfied [BF,COMB], or if the spacetime admits a timelike Killing vector. There is an unsatisfactory gap between these two conditions, which includes the dominant energy condition. Prove a uniqueness theorem for maximal surfaces, assuming only DE.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime of dimension $n+1$ satisfying the dominant energy condition, i.e., for every future-directed causal vector $v$ at every point of $M$, the energy-momentum tensor $T$ (equivalently, via the Einstein equations, the Ricci tensor combined with the scalar curvature) is such that $-T^\mu{}_\nu v^\nu$ is a future-directed causal vector. A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ is called maximal if its mean curvature vanishes identically. It is known that maximal Cauchy surfaces in $(M,g)$ are unique under the stronger timelike convergence condition (i.e., $\mathrm{Ric}(v,v) \geq 0$ for every timelike $v$), and also unique when $(M,g)$ admits a timelike Killing vector field. 

Problem: Prove (or disprove) that under the dominant energy condition alone, any globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ admits at most one maximal Cauchy hypersurface.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a uniqueness theorem for maximal Cauchy surfaces under only the dominant energy condition. Known results in the literature establish uniqueness under the timelike convergence condition (Brill–Flaherty; Marsden–Tipler / Choquet-Bruhat) or in spacetimes with a timelike Killing field, and the gap involving only the dominant energy condition appears not to have been closed.

status_evidence.title: Origins and Development of the Cauchy Problem in General Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of uniqueness results for maximal/CMC surfaces, energy conditions, and the role of TCC versus DEC.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys state uniqueness of maximal Cauchy surfaces under the timelike convergence condition; no analogue under only DEC is reported.

status_evidence.title: Dominant Energy Condition and Spinors on Lorentzian Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys consequences of the DEC; uniqueness of maximal hypersurfaces under DEC alone is not established.
status_evidence.claim: No DEC-only uniqueness theorem for maximal Cauchy surfaces is reported in the literature.
